transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Lately, I keep thinking everyone would be better off without me, and I find myself planning how I might just not be here anymore. A friend from the community center got very worried about me and insisted that I come here to talk to you.
Have you experienced a significant change in your mood or emotional state recently, such as feeling sad, empty, or irritable, that led you to have these thoughts about not being here anymore?

Yes, my mood has been changing a lot—most days I wake up with this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest like a dark cloud, and I feel completely flat and empty. But it also swings, and some weeks I feel strangely high and touchy, snapping at people over nothing. Then I crash back down into feeling so worthless that I just want to disappear so I won't be a burden to anyone anymore.
How long have you been experiencing these mood swings, from the high and touchy feelings to the crashes where you feel worthless and want to disappear?

These mood swings started a little over two years ago after my mother fell seriously ill back in India. The high, wired periods have been coming and going for about a year and eight months, while the heavy, low times when I want to disappear have been happening on and off for about seven months.

Can you describe more about the pattern of your mood swings, specifically how long the high, touchy periods typically last compared to the low, worthless periods, and whether they seem to cycle in any predictable way?

The high, wired phases actually make up the majority of my time over the last two years, coming and going for about a year and eight months. In contrast, the heavy, low periods where I want to disappear have only happened on and off for about seven months in total. I spend almost all my time either sped up or crashing from it, with very few moments in the middle where I feel normal.
Can you estimate how many days or weeks you typically spend in the high, wired state versus the low, worthless state, to help me understand the pattern of your mood swings better?

It is hard to count the exact days, but over the last two years, I have spent the vast majority of my time—about a year and eight months—either in that high, sped-up mode or crashing from it. The heavy, low periods only add up to about seven months in total on and off. This leaves only very short stretches where my mood feels somewhere in the middle.
Do you experience any external triggers or events that seem to consistently precede or follow the shifts between your high, wired states and your low, worthless states?

I'm not really sure of any specific events that trigger the shifts, as they mostly seem to happen on their own. I just know that I always crash hard into a low, empty state right after one of my very active, high periods, and the constant worry about my mother's health is always there in the background.

Can you tell me more about how your high, wired periods end and transition into the low, worthless periods, specifically if there's a noticeable trigger or event that seems to cause the shift from high to low?

There isn't really a specific event or trigger that causes the shift. During those high times, I start so many projects and run around until I completely wear myself and everyone else out. Eventually, I just crash hard and fall right back into that flat, empty feeling.

Can you clarify if your high, wired periods typically last longer than your low, worthless periods, and do these episodes of high and low moods occur in a regular, cyclical pattern, or are they more irregular and unpredictable?

Yes, the high, wired periods definitely last much longer and take up the majority of my time, coming and going for about a year and eight months compared to the low periods which only total about seven months. As for a pattern, they are completely unpredictable and don't follow any regular cycle. They just seem to come and go on and off without any warning.

During your high, wired periods, do you experience any symptoms such as decreased need for sleep, excessive talkativeness, or involvement in activities that have a high potential for painful consequences, like reckless spending or impulsive decisions?

Yes, during those wired times I only sleep about two or three hours a night but I don't feel tired because my mind is racing so fast. I also get caught up in impulsive things, like calling distant relatives in the middle of the night, obsessively cleaning at 3 a.m., and planning big donations to the mosque that I can't actually afford.
Have you ever experienced any episodes where you engaged in impulsive or reckless behaviors during your high, wired periods, such as excessive spending, reckless driving, or risky sexual behavior?

Yes, during those high times I definitely do impulsive things without thinking. I start way too many projects at once and wear everyone out, even messaging old girlfriends in the middle of the night. I also find myself planning big donations to the mosque that I absolutely cannot afford.
Can you tell me if you've ever had a period of time where you felt extremely high or irritable and engaged in impulsive behaviors that lasted for at least four consecutive days, but less than a week?

Yes, I definitely have those high, irritable times where I'm extremely active, cleaning constantly and starting all kinds of projects. However, those phases usually last much longer than just a few days or a week; they typically go on for a few weeks at a time before I finally crash.

Can you confirm if you have ever experienced a distinct period of abnormally elevated or irritable mood that lasted at least 4 consecutive days but less than 2 weeks, which is not necessarily part of your typical longer-lasting high, wired periods?
I'm not really sure about having a specific shorter period like that. Whenever I get into those high, wired states, they always seem to last much longer, usually for several weeks at a time.

Can you recall any instance where you felt extremely high or irritable for at least 4 consecutive days but less than 2 weeks, and during that time, you experienced symptoms like decreased need for sleep, more talkative than usual, or felt like you were invincible, which might be distinct from your usual longer high periods?

I don't think I can recall a specific shorter period like that. When I get into those high, wired states, they always seem to last much longer, usually for weeks at a time, so I'm not sure about a distinct time that was only a few days.

Can you think of any time when you had a shorter period, at least 4 consecutive days but less than 2 weeks, where you felt extremely high or irritable and had symptoms like less need for sleep or excessive talking, separate from your usual longer high periods?
I don't really recall having any shorter periods of just a few days like that. My sped-up or wired phases usually last much longer and have been coming and going over the last year and eight months.

Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely high or irritable, with symptoms like decreased need for sleep or excessive talking, that lasted at least 4 consecutive days but less than 2 weeks, which you can distinguish from your usual longer-lasting high periods?

I'm really not sure, and I don't recall ever having a shorter period of feeling high like that for just four days to two weeks. For me, those sped-up times always seem to last much longer, and I don't remember any distinct short phases separate from them.

Can you think of any instance where you had a period of feeling extremely high or irritable that lasted less than 2 weeks, which might help differentiate between the types of episodes you're experiencing?

When I get into those wired, high phases, I completely lose track of time because my mind is racing so fast. It is really hard for me to say exactly how many days or weeks they last, only that they seem to come and go.
Can you think of any instance where you had a distinct period of feeling extremely high or irritable that lasted less than 4 consecutive days, which might help clarify the nature of your episodes?
I don't recall any times where those high or irritable feelings lasted for such a short time. When those wired periods happen, they usually seem to last much longer than that.
Can you think of any instance where you had a distinct period of feeling extremely high or irritable that lasted less than 4 consecutive days, which might help clarify the nature of your episodes?
No, I don't recall those feelings ever lasting for such a short time. When I get into those high and irritable phases, they usually go on for weeks at a time rather than just a few days.

Can you confirm whether you have experienced any episodes of abnormally elevated or irritable mood that lasted at least 4 consecutive days but less than 2 weeks, which is distinct from your typical longer high periods?

I am really not sure, and I haven't noticed any shorter high periods that only lasted a few days or a couple of weeks. I mostly just remember the much longer, intense phases that have been coming and going over the last couple of years.

Can you confirm if you've ever had a hypomanic episode, which is a period of elevated or irritable mood that lasts at least 4 consecutive days, to help differentiate between bipolar I and bipolar II disorder?

Yes, I definitely experience those high and touchy periods, and they typically last for some weeks, which is well over the four-day mark you mentioned. These wired phases have been happening on and off for about a year and eight months now.

During these high, wired periods that last for weeks, do you experience significant impairment in your social or occupational functioning, or require hospitalization, which could help differentiate between the types of bipolar disorder you might be experiencing?

These high periods have completely disrupted my life and caused a lot of damage. My work has suffered so much that my hours were cut and I am now on a final warning, and I have stopped going to the community center and mosque altogether. I'm also neglecting basic chores and letting bills pile up at home, though I haven't ever been hospitalized for it.

Have you ever been hospitalized due to one of your high, wired periods or low, worthless periods, or have these episodes led to significant problems in your relationships, work, or daily life that you couldn't recover from?

No, I have never been hospitalized, but these episodes have severely ruined my daily life. My work has suffered so much that my hours were cut and I am on a final warning, and I have stopped going to the mosque and community center entirely. At home, I just let the bills and basic chores pile up until someone reminds me or I get a notice.

During your high, wired periods, have you ever experienced symptoms that were so severe they caused you significant distress or impairment in social or occupational functioning, or required hospitalization, which might distinguish between different types of bipolar episodes?

Yes, even though I have never been hospitalized, those high periods have caused major problems. At work, my racing thoughts and snapping at people when criticized led to my hours being cut and getting a final warning. Socially, I wore everyone out by calling at odd hours and making plans I couldn't afford, so I stopped going to the mosque entirely while my chores and bills piled up.

Can you confirm if, during your high, wired periods, you have ever experienced symptoms that were so severe they led to psychotic symptoms, such as hallucinations or delusions, which would be a key factor in distinguishing between different types of bipolar disorder?

Yes, when I get into those wired, high phases, those experiences actually get much worse. The deep voice telling me I'm a failure gets a lot louder, and the feeling that people are sending secret messages about me through their phones and the TV becomes almost constant.

Can you describe more about the deep voice you mentioned, telling you you're a failure, and the feeling that people are sending secret messages about you - are these experiences present during both your high and low periods, or only during one of them?

They definitely get much louder and more constant during my high, wired phases when I'm not sleeping. But they aren't only limited to those times; a few months ago, when my mood felt relatively normal, I still heard that deep voice at night and felt like people were coordinating against me.

Can you confirm if the deep voice and the feeling of people sending secret messages about you are present during your low, worthless periods as well, or if they are exclusively associated with your high, wired phases?

No, they are definitely not exclusive to my high phases. I often hear that deep voice at night when I'm alone and feeling really low, and there was even a stretch a few months ago when my mood felt completely normal but I still heard the voice and felt like people were coordinating against me.

Can you confirm if the deep voice and the feeling of people sending secret messages about you are considered hallucinations or delusions by you, and do they significantly impact your daily functioning or relationships?

I don't really think of them as "hallucinations" or "delusions" because they feel incredibly real to me, even though I know the room is empty when I hear the voice and others say the messages aren't real. But they have a massive impact on my life: my hours at work were cut and I'm on a final warning, I've stopped going to the mosque and community center, and I just let my bills and chores pile up at home.

Can you confirm if the deep voice and the feelings of people sending secret messages about you meet the criteria for hallucinations or delusions, and if they have significantly impacted your daily functioning or relationships during both your high and low periods?

I do hear that deep male voice when I'm alone and believe people are sending secret messages about me through WhatsApp and the TV, which gets much worse when I am high and wired, but it also stayed with me even when my mood was normal. These experiences and my mood swings have severely impacted my life, leading to cut hours and a final warning at work, making me avoid the mosque, and causing me to neglect my bills and chores. It all just feels very real and heavy to deal with.

Can you confirm if the deep voice and the feelings of people sending secret messages about you have ever led to you behaving in ways that put you or others at risk of harm, which could help differentiate between the severity of your episodes?

The deep voice telling me to "go" and the feeling of everyone judging me make me feel so incredibly low that I've mentally planned how to disappear, like imagining walking into the river or stepping in front of a train. However, I haven't actually acted on those plans to hurt myself, and I have never had any thoughts of harming anyone else.

Can you confirm if the deep voice and the feelings of people sending secret messages about you have ever led to you having delusions of grandeur or other psychotic symptoms during your high, wired periods?

Yes, during those high and wired times, the deep voice gets much louder and the feeling that people are sending secret messages about me becomes almost constant. During these same periods, I also feel an intense sense of being chosen for a special mission to cure my mother from here and run the building better than my managers, feeling like I am the only one who can fix everything.
